To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the properties of laser-ablated infinite-layer copper- oxide thin films can be significantly modified by the choice of substrate or buffer-layer material.

(a) the infinite-layer copper oxide films are extremely flat and highly oriented; and (b) the in-plane lattice constant and film thickness can be controlled by substrate or buffer-layer lattice constants.

(1) films of infinite-layer Sr/sub 1-y/La/sub y/CuO/sub x/ were deposited by laser-ablation on substrates or buffer layers of SrTiO/sub x/, La/sub 1+x/Ca/sub 1-x/CuO/sub y/, and Pr/sub 2/CaCuO/sub x/; and (2) films deposited on the latter two buffer-layer materials were electron-doped.

the synthesis of high-quality epitaxial thin films of infinite-layer copper-oxides by pulsed laser-ablation, and with the characterization of these films using a variety of structural and physical-property measurements.
the growth and characterization of thin films of infinite-layer cuprate superconductors by the technique of pulsed laser ablation.
thin film growth, structure and properties of electron-doped infinite-layer compounds.
